name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area composite PMI fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October, still above 50
state: The final HCOB euro-area composite PMI fell to 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September, a four-month low, with services at 51.4, new business near stagnation and France back in contraction (ActionForex, 4 Nov; Trading and Investment News). Growth is slowing but the PMI remains above 50 and no stagnation in GDP has been reported, so the Normal criteria still hold as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Slower growth tends to weigh on hiring and wage gains in the euro area. Exporters and firms selling into France are most exposed.

sources.title: ActionForex — Eurozone PMI composite falls to 51.7 as demand weakens
Trading and Investment News — Euro zone PMI slumps to 4-month low of 51.7

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
